summary.text: Adriel Lam is the Republican nominee and a retired U.S. Army veteran with nearly 24 years of active-duty service, whose family has lived in Hawaii for several generations. He ran for the U.S. Senate Republican nomination in 2024, finishing second in the primary. He says he is running on government accountability, election security, and Hawaii's strategic role in the Pacific.

paragraphs.text: Describes his family's history in Hawaii as spanning generations, including a great-grandfather who arrived in 1872 and a grandfather who worked at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard on the day of the 1941 attack. He names a newspaper route for the South Pasadena Journal as his first job.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington (1993). Ballotpedia lists graduate degrees from Missouri University of Science and Technology (2000), Tarleton State University (2000), the University of Hawaii (2005), and Wayland Baptist University (2024).

Served in the U.S. Army from 1994 to 2018, which he describes as nearly 24 years of active duty, including leading small teams and combat units and enterprise-wide efforts with inter-agency and international partners.
Ran for the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in 2024, receiving 16.5 percent of the vote and finishing second to Bob McDermott.
Ran unopposed in the August 8, 2026 Republican primary for the 1st District.

As of 2024, was listed as a member of organizations including VFW Post 110, the MIS Veterans of Hawaii, the Lions Club of Kaneohe, and the Hawaii Advisory Committee to the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights.
